gap_title: Missing pre‑consent notice and language requirements

gap_title: Missing immediate deletion/cessation on consent withdrawal or purpose expiry
anchor_excerpt: 5.3 The Compliance department owns the Data Subject Request Handling Process, which coordinates the response across Data Engineering, Product Engineering, and Customer Support.
suggested_text: 5.4 Withdrawal‑Triggered Deletion Process. When a Data Principal withdraws consent or the purpose for which personal data was collected ceases to exist, the Compliance department shall immediately halt all processing activities related to that data and initiate an automated deletion workflow. gap_title: Insufficient data accuracy and broader technical safeguards
anchor_excerpt: 6.3 In the event of a confirmed data breach involving personal data, the Information Security department shall notify affected Data Principals and the Data Protection Board of India without undue delay, and in any case within 72 hours of confirming the breach.
suggested_text:
6.4 Data Accuracy and Safeguards

NimbusPay shall implement technical and organisational measures to ensure the accuracy, consistency, and integrity of personal data. These measures include:

• Validation procedures at the point of data entry and during data integration to prevent incorrect or inconsistent data from entering the system.

• Regular consistency checks (at least quarterly) across all data repositories to detect and correct discrepancies.

• Robust access controls, ensuring that only authorised personnel can view or modify personal data, with role‑based permissions and audit logging.

• Continuous monitoring of data quality metrics and automated alerts for anomalies that may indicate data corruption or tampering.

• Periodic risk assessments (at least annually) to identify and mitigate risks to data accuracy, including the impact of system changes, third‑party integrations, and emerging threats.

These safeguards complement existing encryption controls and are designed to meet the requirements of Section 8 of applicable data protection law.

The Compliance department shall develop and maintain a Penalty Management Policy that defines the calculation of monetary penalties for data‑breach violations. The policy will specify:

gap_title: No mechanism to provide information to Central Government on request
suggested_text:
8.1.1 Government Information Request Procedure

When the Central Government or any authorized regulatory authority issues a formal request for information regarding NimbusPay’s data processing activities, the Compliance department shall:

1. Verify the authenticity and legal basis of the request, ensuring it complies with Section 36 of the applicable law.
2. Notify the Data Protection Officer (if appointed) and relevant stakeholders within 48 hours of receipt.
3. Collect the requested data in a secure, tamper‑evident manner, preserving audit trails.
4. Provide the information in the format specified by the requesting authority, no later than 30 days from receipt of the request, unless an extension is granted by the authority.
5. Document all steps taken, including validation, data extraction, and delivery, and retain the documentation for a minimum of 8 years.
6. Report the request and response to the Data Protection Board of India as required by law.

The Compliance department owns this procedure and shall review it annually or upon significant regulatory changes.

gap_title: No controls for handling government‑issued blocking orders
anchor_excerpt: 8.2 This policy does not currently designate a named Data Protection Officer responsible for overseeing NimbusPay's compliance with applicable data protection law.
suggested_text:
8.3 Blocking Order Compliance Process

8.3.1 Purpose
The purpose of this process is to ensure that NimbusPay complies with any government‑issued blocking orders (Section 37) and that such orders are logged, verified, and acted upon in a timely manner by all relevant departments.

8.3.2 Scope
This process applies to all NimbusPay employees, contractors, and third‑party vendors who receive or handle personal data on behalf of NimbusPay.

8.3.3 Ownership
The Compliance department owns the Blocking Order Compliance Process and is responsible for maintaining the Blocking Order Log, coordinating responses, and reporting to the relevant authorities.

8.3.4 Logging and Verification
Upon receipt of a blocking order, the Compliance department must:
• Log the order in the Blocking Order Log, recording the order reference, date received, affected data categories, and any instructions.
• Verify the authenticity of the order by confirming it originates from a recognized government authority.

8.3.5 Response Actions
If the order requires data restriction, deletion, or disclosure, the Compliance department shall:
• Notify the Information Security department to implement technical controls (e.g., access restrictions, data masking) within 48 hours.
• Coordinate with the Data Engineering department to isolate or delete the affected data within 7 days of verification.
• Ensure that any required notifications to affected Data Principals or regulatory bodies are made within the timelines specified in Section 6.3.

8.3.6 Documentation and Review
All actions taken in response to a blocking order must be documented in the Blocking Order Log. The Compliance department will review the log quarterly to ensure compliance and will report findings to senior management.

8.3.7 Training
All employees who may receive or act upon a blocking order will receive annual training on this process and the legal obligations under Section 37.
